description: VyralX script-quality library: lanes, hook formulas, format structures, escalation and payoff patterns, and the scoring rubric used by app/services/script_quality.py. The scriptwriter (app/services/content.py) reads its brief from this file; the scorer grades every generated script against it BEFORE production. Edit this file to retune the system - no code change needed.

one_fact.label: One fact
rules: Exactly one central claim; every beat serves it.
The mechanism beat is mandatory - a fact without a why is a caption, not a video.
End on the payoff, never on a summary.
structure: mechanism - how or why it is true

story.label: Story
rules: Open at the most dramatic moment, then rewind.
At least two turns (but / until / suddenly) before the climax.
The payoff line must call back to the cold open.

top5.label: Top 5 countdown
rules: Count DOWN from 5 to 1; number 1 must be the item teased in the hook.
Each entry is bigger, stranger or costlier than the one before it.
One line per entry wherever possible - entries are beats, not paragraphs.

examples.history_facts: This empire lasted 500 years longer than you think.
examples.space_science: This star is 5 billion times brighter than you think.
examples.tech_ai: This chip does 100 trillion calculations more per second than you think.

hook_formulas.name: Number shock
hook_formulas.template: This {subject} is {number} times {comparison} than you think.

examples.history_facts: Why did Roman soldiers carry vinegar into battle?
examples.tech_ai: Why does your phone listen even when it is off?

examples.history_facts: The Great Wall is not what you think it is.
examples.space_science: The Moon is not what you think it is.
examples.tech_ai: Your passwords are not stored the way you think.

hook_formulas.name: Myth negation
hook_formulas.template: {Subject} is not what you think it is.

examples.history_facts: Five inventions older than you think - number one is a computer.
examples.space_science: Five moons stranger than ours - and number one rains diamonds.
examples.tech_ai: Five things your phone tracks daily - number three is illegal in Europe.

examples.history_facts: 79 AD. Pompeii. A baker put bread in the oven.
examples.space_science: 1969. The Moon. One astronaut stayed behind, alone.
examples.tech_ai: 2010. A programmer paid 10,000 bitcoin for two pizzas.

examples.history_facts: If history were one day, writing appears in the last minute.

examples.tech_ai: If this AI read all day, it would finish the internet by lunch.

examples.tech_ai: You unlock your phone 100 times a day - but it never sees your face.

history_facts.audience: Global English-speaking general-knowledge audience, including Indian history and world history; archive-led (Wikimedia / Internet Archive public domain).
history_facts.label: History & did-you-know
history_facts.promise: A true story or fact from the past that reframes something the viewer thought they knew.
source_types: Wikimedia Commons public-domain imagery and footage

space_science.audience: Global English-speaking curiosity audience; footage-led (NASA/NOAA/ESA public domain).
banned_terms: nasa doesn't want you to know
nasa does not want you to know
space_science.label: Space & science
space_science.promise: One true, mind-expanding fact about the universe, proven on screen, in under a minute.

tech_ai.audience: Global English-speaking tech-curious audience; led by own screen recordings and short review/demo clips.
tech_ai.label: Tech & AI explainers
tech_ai.promise: One piece of technology the viewer uses or hears about daily, explained so simply it clicks in under a minute.
source_types: own screen recordings of the product or model in use
short review/demo clips used under review exceptions with commentary
vendor press footage credited on screen

payoffs.name: Callback
payoffs.rule: The final beat reuses a content word or image from the hook, closing the loop the hook opened.

payoffs.name: Scale landing
payoffs.rule: The final beat carries the biggest number or comparison in the script.

payoffs.name: Implication
payoffs.rule: The final beat states what the fact means for the viewer (markers: 'which means', 'so the next time', 'that is why', 'that's why').

payoffs.name: Loop close
payoffs.rule: The final beat echoes the hook's opening words so the Short loops seamlessly into a rewatch.

payoffs.name: Verdict line
payoffs.rule: A short closing sentence (8 words or fewer) that delivers the outcome or judgement, mainly for story format.
